title: Personal Checking Tier Entry Thresholds
content:
Every Personal Checking tier sets the smallest first deposit that funds and activates a new account, the relationship balance the customer must already hold on the opening date, the age range in whole years on the opening date at which the customer may open the tier as sole owner, and the largest number of open accounts of that same tier one customer may hold as primary owner.

| Tier | Smallest first deposit (USD) | Relationship balance required on the opening date (USD) | Youngest age to open (whole years) | Oldest age to open (whole years) | Most open accounts of this tier per customer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 25.00 | 0.00 | 18 | no maximum | 1 |
| Student Checking | 25.00 | 0.00 | 17 | 24 | 1 |
| Everyday Checking | 50.00 | 0.00 | 18 | no maximum | 4 |
| Interest Checking | 100.00 | 0.00 | 18 | no maximum | 4 |
| Premier Checking | 100.00 | 0.00 | 18 | no maximum | 2 |
| Private Client Checking | 100.00 | 250000.00 | 18 | no maximum | 2 |

A relationship balance figure of 0.00 means the tier carries no relationship requirement at all. Where the oldest age reads as no maximum, the tier sets no upper age at opening.

**Reading the age range.** Student Checking is the only tier that closes at the top: a customer aged 24 in whole years on the opening date is inside its range, and a customer aged 25 is outside it. Every other tier opens at 18 and runs upward without a ceiling, so a customer aged 17 in whole years meets no tier's youngest age except Student Checking.
